nodes.norm_label: gotcha: seaorm insert_many cannot mix set and notset for the same column

nodes.community_name: Gotcha: Config Env Overrides — Null Replaces, JSON Quoting, Zero-Padded Numbers

nodes.label: Gotcha: Config Env Overrides — Null Replaces, JSON Quoting, Zero-Padded Numbers
nodes.community_name: Gotcha: Config Env Overrides — Null Replaces, JSON Quoting, Zero-Padded Numbers
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: config env overrides — null replaces, json quoting, zero-padded numbers
nodes.rationale: null replaces a value but never removes a key, deliberately: fields like api_url are Option without serde(default), so removing the key would produce missing field errors; null for a whole entry is a startup error because deletion via env is unsupported. Values parse as JSON first with a plain-string fallback, so NAME=123 injects a number and a literal string needs '"123"'; zero-padded 06 is invalid JSON and silently becomes a string. Serde errors reference the merged JSON, not the offending var — the applied config env override info logs list every var and its path, and raw values stay out of info level because RPC URLs may embed API keys.

nodes.label: Gotcha: Filter Params Must Not Reuse Pagination Cursor Field Names
nodes.community_name: Gotcha: Filter Params Must Not Reuse Pagination Cursor Field Names
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: filter params must not reuse pagination cursor field names
nodes.rationale: GetMessagesRequest/GetTransfersRequest and their byTx/byAddress variants already use bridge_id as a raw pagination cursor (proto field 7), and GetChainsStatsRequest uses chain_id (field 8) the same way, so a read filter with either name collides with cursor semantics for api.use_pagination_token=false clients. The unified read-filter vocabulary — home_chain_id, counterparty_chain_ids, bridge_ids — avoids the collision by construction.

nodes.label: Gotcha: Unknown Query Params Are Silently Ignored by Generated HTTP Routes
nodes.community_name: Gotcha: Filter Params Must Not Reuse Pagination Cursor Field Names
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: unknown query params are silently ignored by generated http routes
nodes.rationale: #[actix_prost_macros::serde] expands to a plain derive without deny_unknown_fields (verified in actix-prost-macros 0.3.1), so generated routes drop undeclared query params. An endpoint therefore cannot reject a filter it does not declare, and a client passing an unsupported filter silently receives unfiltered data — for per-frontend slicing that leaks other bridges'/chains' rows. The pattern is to declare the field in proto even when unsupported and return Status::invalid_argument for non-blank values.

nodes.community_name: ADR-007: The Scan Floor Is Reconciled Against The Checkpoint, Not Against bridge_contracts (Accepted, with stated expiry)
nodes.norm_label: neutral consequence: bridge_contracts returns to being purely diagnostic

nodes.label: catchup_max_cursor is deliberately untouched — lowering a floor causes no rescan in the current design
nodes.community_name: ADR-007: The Scan Floor Is Reconciled Against The Checkpoint, Not Against bridge_contracts (Accepted, with stated expiry)
nodes.norm_label: catchup_max_cursor is deliberately untouched — lowering a floor causes no rescan in the current design
nodes.rationale: A completed catch-up already left catchup_max_cursor at old_floor - 1 via mark_catchup_complete, which is exactly where the reopened descending scan resumes, and a catch-up still in progress has it above the old floor and keeps walking past it. Writing it would therefore be a no-op at best and re-scan one extra block at worst.

nodes.label: Disabled bridges are reconciled too
nodes.community_name: ADR-007: The Scan Floor Is Reconciled Against The Checkpoint, Not Against bridge_contracts (Accepted, with stated expiry)
nodes.rationale: A bridge can be lowered while disabled and re-enabled later, nothing indexes it in the meantime, and enumerate_indexing_targets still excludes it from the endpoint — so reconciling it is free and keeps the invariant true whenever it is re-enabled.

nodes.label: Expiry condition: when catch-up becomes bidirectional this function must be replaced, not extended
nodes.community_name: ADR-007: The Scan Floor Is Reconciled Against The Checkpoint, Not Against bridge_contracts (Accepted, with stated expiry)
nodes.norm_label: expiry condition: when catch-up becomes bidirectional this function must be replaced, not extended
nodes.rationale: If catchup_min_cursor becomes the ascending frontier, configured_floor < stored is true whenever the walk has made any progress, so an unconditional lower fires every startup and resets the walk — a loop, not a one-off rescan; the naive guard 'only lower when catch-up is still in progress' is exactly the broken branch. The replacement is Alternative 2 plus setting catchup_max_cursor = old_floor - 1 to confine the rescan to the newly opened range. Whoever does that must also make the write's failure fatal for the pair, because under a bidirectional indexer the identical failure would silently drop the newly opened range instead of merely misreporting a percentage.

nodes.label: The identity-set-change bug: a new (address, version) makes the derived previous floor None, so nothing is lowered and the progress report is permanently 100%
nodes.community_name: ADR-007: The Scan Floor Is Reconciled Against The Checkpoint, Not Against bridge_contracts (Accepted, with stated expiry)
nodes.norm_label: the identity-set-change bug: a new (address, version) makes the derived previous floor none, so nothing is lowered and the progress report is permanently 100%
nodes.rationale: The original pass reconstructed the previous run's floor from bridge_contracts.started_at_block to act only on a detected transition. That works for an in-place edit and fails for a change to the identity set: a new entry has no stored row, so the derived previous floor is None ('unknown'), deliberately not treated as a change — and the same startup's upsert_bridge_contracts then writes the rows, so the derived floor equals the configured floor forever. The scan itself was never wrong (genesis_block comes from config) but the report was permanently wrong: lo = max(catchup_min_cursor, start_block) = 1000 against catchup_max_cursor = 999 answers scan_complete = true, 0 remaining, 100% for the whole rescan and after. The deeper problem is that bridge_contracts is a proxy — the needed quantity is the pair's previous floor, but the table stores per-contract values whose identity set can change underneath the derivation.

nodes.label: Negative consequence: a workaround licensed by a current invariant, not a general solution
nodes.community_name: ADR-007: The Scan Floor Is Reconciled Against The Checkpoint, Not Against bridge_contracts (Accepted, with stated expiry)
nodes.norm_label: negative consequence: a workaround licensed by a current invariant, not a general solution
nodes.rationale: Correctness rests entirely on catchup_min_cursor being a stored floor rather than a frontier, a property enforced by no type or constraint — only by the fact that no writer advances it. The pass also no longer distinguishes 'configuration changed' from 'stored value diverged otherwise'; both are corrected identically, which is the intent, but the logs now report only the write, not a transition.

nodes.community_name: ADR-007: The Scan Floor Is Reconciled Against The Checkpoint, Not Against bridge_contracts (Accepted, with stated expiry)
nodes.norm_label: the 'reconcile before upsert_bridge_contracts' ordering hazard is gone
nodes.rationale: The old doc comment warned that reordering breaks detection with no test failure unless the ordering itself is asserted. Since bridge_contracts is no longer read there is no order left to get wrong, and a test asserts the inverse property. The ordering rule had held in the failing case anyway and bought nothing, because the evidence was already absent rather than overwritten.

nodes.label: Gotcha: AMB Home/Foreign Side Comes From Proxy ABI Events
nodes.community_name: ADR-007: The Scan Floor Is Reconciled Against The Checkpoint, Not Against bridge_contracts (Accepted, with stated expiry)
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: amb home/foreign side comes from proxy abi events
nodes.rationale: Side inference from the ABI event set (Foreign: UserRequestForAffirmation + RelayedMessage; Home: UserRequestForSignature, AffirmationCompleted, validator signature events, CollectedSignatures) keeps AMB configs free of hardcoded Ethereum/Gnosis chain IDs, so non-mainnet deployments work unchanged. nodes.label: Gotcha: The AMB Scan Floor Is The amb_proxy Contract's started_at_block
nodes.community_name: ADR-007: The Scan Floor Is Reconciled Against The Checkpoint, Not Against bridge_contracts (Accepted, with stated expiry)
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: the amb scan floor is the amb_proxy contract's started_at_block
nodes.rationale: AMB declares two contracts per (bridge, chain) but one log stream covers both addresses, and the floor comes from amb_proxy alone — taking min across all a chain's contracts would understate it by ~7.4M blocks on chain 1, where the mediator sits far below the proxy. ChainPlan/plan_bridge is the single selection rule feeding the progress denominator, genesis_block, and startup floor reconciliation; adding a second derivation site is the hazard to avoid. min rather than 'the first one' because several versions of one kind is how a contract upgrade is expressed. An AMB chain with no amb_proxy yields no floor at all, because a plausible number for a scan that never runs is worse than none. A mediator floor above the proxy floor is legal (AMB-only operation), a missing mediator is legal, but a configured mediator with a broken ABI stays fatal because that is a config error rather than a choice.

nodes.label: Gotcha: bridge_contracts Is Only A Diagnostic Proxy For Runtime Membership
nodes.community_name: ADR-007: The Scan Floor Is Reconciled Against The Checkpoint, Not Against bridge_contracts (Accepted, with stated expiry)
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: bridge_contracts is only a diagnostic proxy for runtime membership
nodes.rationale: The table is written by upsert_bridge_contracts at startup, intentionally sequenced after the stats backfill pass, so it is under-populated exactly when backfill needs an accurate indexed-chain set. It is also permanently over-populated after a chain is removed from a bridge, because no code path deletes a row when bridges.json drops a contract. The authoritative answer is always IndexedChains::may_observe built from in-memory config.

nodes.label: Gotcha: Bridge Name Cache Has No Negative Caching
nodes.community_name: ADR-007: The Scan Floor Is Reconciled Against The Checkpoint, Not Against bridge_contracts (Accepted, with stated expiry)
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: bridge name cache has no negative caching
nodes.rationale: InterchainDatabase caches known bridge names but not 'not found', so a non-existent bridge ID re-queries the database on every lookup. Accepted because bridge IDs in messages are expected to exist; negative caching is only worth adding if it becomes a measured performance problem.

nodes.label: Gotcha: catchup_min_cursor Is A Stored Floor, Not A Frontier — And Code Depends On That
nodes.community_name: ADR-007: The Scan Floor Is Reconciled Against The Checkpoint, Not Against bridge_contracts (Accepted, with stated expiry)
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: catchup_min_cursor is a stored floor, not a frontier — and code depends on that
nodes.rationale: The name suggests a moving lower boundary symmetric with catchup_max_cursor, but it never advances with progress: upsert_cursors always supplies 0 and relies on GREATEST(existing, 0) purely to preserve what is stored, and exactly two writers move it — seed_catchup_floor (raise-only) and lower_catchup_floor (lower-only). reconcile_catchup_floors is licensed by precisely that; make it a frontier and the same comparison becomes true whenever the ascending walk progressed, turning a one-off rescan into a loop on every restart. The tell that you are breaking this: you are adding a writer that raises catchup_min_cursor for a reason other than a configuration change.

nodes.label: Gotcha: A Contract Version Is (address, block), Not address
nodes.community_name: ADR-007: The Scan Floor Is Reconciled Against The Checkpoint, Not Against bridge_contracts (Accepted, with stated expiry)
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: a contract version is (address, block), not address
nodes.rationale: An AMB proxy is upgraded behind the same address, so address alone cannot identify the implementation — and neither can topic0, which hashes the event signature without recording which parameters are indexed, so two versions can share a topic and decode differently. Hence UNIQUE(bridge_id, chain_id, address, version) plus started_at_block, and resolution at decode time via AbiRegistry::resolve_log. Deliberately not fixed by splitting eth_getLogs into per-version windows: narrowing the fetch would have to be mirrored exactly by the retry path, and a replay narrower than the forward scan resolves holes it never re-read. A log whose topic belongs to a different version window than its block is dropped and counted by interchain_indexer_amb_logs_dropped_wrong_version_total — non-zero means a started_at_block disagrees with the chain and real events are discarded with no ledger row, because the blocks were scanned.

nodes.label: Gotcha: Lowering A Scan Floor Does Not Cause A Rescan
nodes.community_name: ADR-007: The Scan Floor Is Reconciled Against The Checkpoint, Not Against bridge_contracts (Accepted, with stated expiry)
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: lowering a scan floor does not cause a rescan
nodes.rationale: The descending catch-up resumes from catchup_max_cursor, which a completed catch-up left at old_floor - 1 — exactly the top of the newly opened range — and an in-progress catch-up simply walks past the old floor to the new one, so only [new_floor, old_floor - 1] is fetched. Reconciliation deliberately does not touch catchup_max_cursor, since writing it would be a no-op at best and re-fetch a block at worst. The asymmetric case does rescan: raising a floor lets catch-up complete above it, so later restoring the floor re-fetches the range between the two floors (rows re-derived, not duplicated).

nodes.label: Gotcha: started_at_block = NULL Means "Index from Genesis"
nodes.community_name: ADR-007: The Scan Floor Is Reconciled Against The Checkpoint, Not Against bridge_contracts (Accepted, with stated expiry)
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: started_at_block = null means "index from genesis"
nodes.rationale: bridge_contracts.started_at_block is nullable and None maps to .unwrap_or(0) in BridgeContractConfig, so NULL is the expected encoding of 'from genesis' and should not warn. Set the value only for non-genesis starts.

nodes.label: Gotcha: Stats Eligibility Is About Observability, Not Protocol Terminality
nodes.community_name: ADR-007: The Scan Floor Is Reconciled Against The Checkpoint, Not Against bridge_contracts (Accepted, with stated expiry)
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: stats eligibility is about observability, not protocol terminality
nodes.rationale: Eligibility answers exactly one question — can the missing evidence still arrive? — which is true exactly when the chain that would produce it is indexed by that bridge. Judging by status = Completed defers unobservable messages forever; judging by protocol terminality alone freezes a singleton asset that a later source-side upsert can never revisit. Nothing in the rule may branch on bridge type. The indexed set must come from in-memory config, never bridge_contracts, because startup backfill runs before upsert_bridge_contracts. may_observe is permissive for an absent bridge (map_or(true, ..), not is_some_and) so removing a bridge from config commits and hides nothing. Counting (stats_processed, additive and never reversed) is separate from identity maintenance (idempotent, may re-run).

nodes.label: Gotcha (RESOLVED): Stats Transfer Backfill Matched Failed AMB Projection Eligibility
nodes.community_name: ADR-007: The Scan Floor Is Reconciled Against The Checkpoint, Not Against bridge_contracts (Accepted, with stated expiry)
nodes.norm_label: gotcha (resolved): stats transfer backfill matched failed amb projection eligibility
nodes.rationale: Resolved by m20260720_120000_add_read_filters_and_bridge_stats. Backfill used to filter parents to Completed only while live projection also accepted failed AMB, so a full rebuild silently dropped failed-AMB aggregates. The invariant now is a single shared eligibility predicate, finalized_message_stats_condition() exposed pub(crate), called by both the message and transfer backfill queries — one predicate is the only way live and historical paths cannot drift.

nodes.label: upsert_cursors — GREATEST-only cursor maintenance writer (cannot lower a floor)
nodes.norm_label: upsert_cursors — greatest-only cursor maintenance writer (cannot lower a floor)
nodes.rationale: Because upsert_cursors applies GREATEST it can only raise, which is exactly why the downward direction must be owned by a startup pass, and why always supplying 0 preserves rather than advances the stored floor.

nodes.label: Gotcha: Cross-Bridge Resolver Persistence Leaks (BlockchainIdResolver global cache)
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: cross-bridge resolver persistence leaks (blockchainidresolver global cache)
nodes.rationale: The resolver cache and its writes to chains / avalanche_icm_blockchain_ids are global while the filtering decision is per-bridge, so a permissive bridge's discovery lets a strict bridge skip a Data API call. Benign — the strict bridge still applies its own chain_ids set and rejects the message. No fix needed; just read the chains table as the union of all bridges' discovery activity.

nodes.label: Gotcha: Events Filtered for Unconfigured Chains (process_unknown_chains + home_chain_id)
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: events filtered for unconfigured chains (process_unknown_chains + home_chain_id)
nodes.rationale: Two sequential bridge-level filters run before the buffer, so filtered messages never reach consolidation or the database at all. Both endpoints unknown always skip; one-known/one-unknown needs process_unknown_chains: true; a set home_chain_id requires at least one endpoint to equal it. Filtering ahead of the buffer is deliberate — it keeps unwanted data out of every downstream layer rather than filtering at read time.

nodes.label: Gotcha: pending_messages Retention for Unconfigured Counterparts Is Load-Bearing, Not a Leak
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: pending_messages retention for unconfigured counterparts is load-bearing, not a leak
nodes.rationale: Removal is gated on protocol finality, not on 'has this key been flushed', so a Partial flush keeps its cold-tier row permanently when the counterpart chain is unconfigured. Deliberate: consolidation reads only buffered state and cannot rehydrate a canonical row, consolidate() refuses to fabricate a message for a configured source chain with no send yet, and the retained row is the only place destination-side information still lives — which is what makes adding a chain to a bridge later safe without rescanning the already-indexed chain past its checkpoint. The retained entry is needed to trigger re-consolidation, not because information is missing: from_send consumes only seven fields the canonical row already stores. Distinguish 'still catching up' from 'permanently retained' by sampling the oldest timestamp per (bridge_id, chain_id) twice.

nodes.label: Gotcha: Upgrading Unknown Chains to Proper Bridges (delete + re-index, don't upgrade in place)
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: upgrading unknown chains to proper bridges (delete + re-index, don't upgrade in place)
nodes.rationale: Messages from unknown chains are stored with init_timestamp = last_update_timestamp and no src_tx_hash; re-indexing the source chain alone would have the upsert overwrite destination-side data with incomplete source-only data. Clean delete plus fresh re-index under a new strict bridge is simpler and safer than incremental upgrade. The production model is strict per-pair bridges plus one permissive monitoring bridge pinned by home_chain_id.

nodes.label: Missing Post-getLogs Acknowledgement Boundary
nodes.rationale: LogStream treats eth_getLogs Ok(...) as scan completion and receives no consumer acknowledgement, so a range whose downstream processing failed leaves no hot barrier and a later cold item can bridge across it; a checkpoint therefore certifies scanning, not correctness.

nodes.label: Counting and Identity Are Separate Concerns
nodes.norm_label: counting and identity are separate concerns
nodes.rationale: stats_processed guards counting only (additive, exactly once, never reversed), while asset/token identity maintenance is idempotent and must run for every flushed key including Partial ones, or a later relink filling a missing token endpoint would be silently missed.

nodes.label: Gotcha: abi_decode_validate Does Not Reject Trailing Bytes
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: abi_decode_validate does not reject trailing bytes
nodes.rationale: alloy_sol_types::SolValue::abi_decode_validate only type-checks the tokens it reads and never verifies the input slice was fully consumed, so non-canonical offsets and trailing garbage both pass. The explicit canonicity round trip — re-encode and compare byte-for-byte — is the layer that actually rejects them. It matters here because a false-positive ICTT payload decode would fabricate a bogus crosschain_transfers row from an arbitrary ICM message.

nodes.label: Gotcha: Message Finality is Complex — ICM payload kind decides ICTT completeness
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: message finality is complex — icm payload kind decides ictt completeness

Both stayed Partial forever and never left pending_messages. Discriminating on the decoded TeleporterMessage payload kind (SINGLE_HOP_SEND/CALL still wait; REGISTER_REMOTE/MULTI_HOP_SEND/CALL complete on available evidence) is what lets completeness rest on the evidence that can actually exist.

nodes.label: ICTT Credit Expectation Classification
nodes.rationale: ICTT completeness is not both-sides-present: SINGLE_HOP_* expects a destination credit while REGISTER_REMOTE / MULTI_HOP_* never will get one, so classifying no-credit-expected as complete closes the bug where unindexed-source and multi-hop-first-leg messages stayed Partial forever.

nodes.label: Gotcha: AMB Collision Replacement Must Delete Before Insert
nodes.community_name: Gotcha: Recoverable Message Fields Are Not A "Never Mirror" Case
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: amb collision replacement must delete before insert
nodes.rationale: COALESCE-and-merge is right for out-of-order enrichment but wrong for a confirmed messageId collision: the stored row belongs to a different AMB body and must not be enriched. Collision-produced rows request replacement — the maintenance flush deletes the (id, bridge_id) row first, relying on FK cascade, then inserts the executed body and anomaly rows in one transaction.

nodes.label: Gotcha: AMB Source and Destination Events Can Arrive Out of Order
nodes.community_name: Gotcha: Recoverable Message Fields Are Not A "Never Mirror" Case
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: amb source and destination events can arrive out of order
nodes.rationale: AMB merges independent chain streams, so transfer reconstruction must never require both sides at once. Each side is persisted as observed and the row is built from whichever sides are present. Persistence must preserve the same order independence: crosschain_transfers conflict handling merges nullable side columns instead of blind-updating, or a late partial side clears data already extracted from the opposite-side event.

nodes.label: Gotcha: AMB Header Sender Is Not The Source Transaction Initiator
nodes.community_name: Gotcha: Recoverable Message Fields Are Not A "Never Mirror" Case
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: amb header sender is not the source transaction initiator
nodes.rationale: AMB header sender/executor are protocol identity fields needed for matching and collision detection, but they are not the source transaction initiator — receipt.from is, and the shared EVM receipt helper drops it before AMB dispatch. Symmetrically, the AMB message destination is the message executor, not the Omnibridge transfer recipient: TokensBridged.recipient belongs to the transfer row only. Existing rows need reindexing to change.

nodes.label: Gotcha: AMB Transfer Sides Are Nullable and Never Mirrored
nodes.community_name: Gotcha: Recoverable Message Fields Are Not A "Never Mirror" Case
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: amb transfer sides are nullable and never mirrored
nodes.rationale: The old NOT NULL columns forced the indexer to substitute the only token it had into both sides; that token came from AMB calldata and is source-token for handleBridgedTokens* but destination-token for handleNativeTokens*, so mirroring conflated the sides and corrupted stats. Making the four columns nullable and populating each side only from its own event means token_src_address == token_dst_address now denotes a genuine same-address pair rather than a placeholder. Go-forward only; the down migration backfills a zero sentinel rather than re-mirroring.

nodes.label: Gotcha: recipient_address On A Terminal crosschain_messages Row Can Never Be Patched Later
nodes.community_name: Gotcha: Recoverable Message Fields Are Not A "Never Mirror" Case
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: recipient_address on a terminal crosschain_messages row can never be patched later
nodes.rationale: crosschain_messages_on_conflict applies per-column merge policies, not one uniform one. dst_chain_id, dst_tx_hash and recipient_address use keep_existing_if_terminal — once status is completed/failed the stored value wins unconditionally, even a stored NULL over an incoming non-NULL. sender_address, payload and src_tx_hash use prefer_incoming (COALESCE) and therefore self-heal. That asymmetry is why recipient_address must be populated at first write on the unindexed-source fallback path: 'a later send will patch it' is false for exactly this column.

nodes.label: Gotcha: Recoverable Message Fields Are Not A "Never Mirror" Case
nodes.community_name: Gotcha: Recoverable Message Fields Are Not A "Never Mirror" Case
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: recoverable message fields are not a "never mirror" case
nodes.rationale: The test is whether a value is ambiguous or merely late. ADR-003 forbids copying one side's value into the other side's column when the true value is genuinely unknown and directionally ambiguous — its motivating case is AMB calldata _token, which means source or destination token depending on the mediator function. Reading originSenderAddress / destinationAddress / message out of a delivered Warp-verified ICM message is not mirroring: those are unambiguously named fields the message carries about itself, observed from an equally authoritative point. src_tx_hash is the one field this does not rescue — it is a fact about a transaction on a never-observed chain and must stay NULL. Commit 9329320c wrongly codified the NULLs as an invariant with a test and comment.

nodes.label: Gotcha: The Retry Pass Starves The Forward Streams, And That Looks Like RPC Failure
nodes.community_name: Indexing Gaps, Retries, and Checkpoint Safety
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: the retry pass starves the forward streams, and that looks like rpc failure
nodes.rationale: RangeDriver::run is one task with one tokio::select!, and run_retry_tick is awaited inside a branch, so the stream.next() branch is not polled while the pass runs. The pause is max_chunks_per_pass x per-chunk latency — a bound in chunks, not in time. The TimedOut burst is a consequence, not a cause: forward requests registered their deadlines before the pass, their timers fire while the task is busy, and the first poll after the pass returns TimedOut — 2N warnings for N chains in the same millisecond is the signature. Keeping max_chunks_per_pass low (default 2) costs replay throughput and never coverage because the sweep resumes on the next tick; the real fix (time-bounding the pass or moving it off the driver task) would introduce process() running concurrently with the forward path and is a design change of the class ADR-005 rejected.

nodes.label: Gotcha: Stats Asset Mapping Conflicts Merge; Only Same-Chain Collisions Skip
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: stats asset mapping conflicts merge; only same-chain collisions skip
nodes.rationale: Asset identity is an incrementally discovered connected-component problem — disjoint components {A,B} and {C,D} are legitimate until a later B->C transfer joins them — so merging is the correct default rather than a conflict. merge_assets is a transactional weighted validate-then-mutate union in the same transaction as the triggering transfer. The one genuine refusal is a merge that would put two different tokens of one chain into one stats_asset, because that cannot be forced without corrupting the chain-uniqueness invariant. Decimals conflict is a separate non-corrupting skip on the counting path only, and never aborts the batch. Skipped rows are marked processed so they do not re-warn every cycle.

nodes.label: Gotcha: Token Identity In stats_asset_tokens Is The ICTT Contract Address, Not The Wrapped ERC-20
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: token identity in stats_asset_tokens is the ictt contract address, not the wrapped erc-20
nodes.rationale: Intentional modelling: ICTT keys chain-local token identity by the TokenTransferrer (Home/Remote bridge) contract address, not the wrapped ERC-20. When Home and Remote are deployed at the same address via CREATE2 the two chain-local rows legitimately carry the same address — one asset on two chains, not a collision. Owner-confirmed (observed on NUMI/WTTC). Do not eyeball address equality; use the split detector, which correctly does not flag it.

nodes.label: Pre-Buffer Storage Gate
nodes.rationale: Filtering runs before buffer.alter() so rejected events never contribute touched_blocks, checkpoints, consolidation, or persistence; the indexed set is frozen at startup because dynamic expansion would require mid-run changes to streams, checkpoints, and provider pools.

nodes.label: A failed floor write stays a warn (today)
nodes.norm_label: a failed floor write stays a warn (today)
nodes.rationale: It is not a lost change any more, because the next startup re-enforces the agreement — the pass asserts an invariant instead of detecting a transition. It is tolerable because the descending scan takes its floor from the config value handed to LogStream.genesis_block and ignores catchup_min_cursor entirely, so the cost is a misreported percentage and no lost data. ADR-005 records why that must change under a bidirectional indexer.

nodes.label: Gotcha: AMB Queued Events Must Preserve Their Emitting Chain
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: amb queued events must preserve their emitting chain
nodes.rationale: Cursor attribution must follow the physical log source chain, not the AMB header source/destination or the context that drains a pending message_hash queue. Otherwise a Gnosis block number is persisted as Ethereum's realtime_cursor and Ethereum realtime polling waits forever behind a cursor above its own latest block.

nodes.label: Gotcha: A Checkpoint Certifies Scanning, Not Correctness
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: a checkpoint certifies scanning, not correctness
nodes.rationale: A checkpoint records that eth_getLogs returned for a range plus inferred empty gaps — never that every covered block was processed without error, since a range that failed downstream leaves no hot barrier and a later item moves the frontier across it. Completeness lives in indexer_failures; in the API, failed_blocks != 0 is the only completeness signal and the percentage is the scanned share by design. The converse does not hold either: failed_blocks == 0 means nothing was recorded, and a swallowed handler error is invisible while a replay over that range reads as success and resolves the hole. Propagating the failure is what buys the guarantee; alert on interchain_indexer_oldest_open_hole_age_seconds because the retry pass is the only recovery path.

nodes.label: Gotcha: Checkpoint Stall When All Events Are Perpetually Filtered
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: checkpoint stall when all events are perpetually filtered
nodes.rationale: Checkpoint advancement is driven by touched_blocks recorded during buffer.alter(); if every event is filtered there is no alter() and the checkpoint never moves. No livelock at runtime because LogStream progresses in memory — the only cost is replayed RPC calls after a restart. Accepted as benign and self-correcting; mitigation is config hygiene (drop the pair from bridge contracts) rather than code.

nodes.label: Gotcha: The Failure Ledger's Healthy Path Is DB-Free Only Because One Process Owns A Bridge
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: the failure ledger's healthy path is db-free only because one process owns a bridge
nodes.rationale: FailureLedger keeps an in-memory set of pairs with open holes so a healthy batch issues zero statements; the cache may be stale-true (one redundant query) but must never be stale-false, which holds only under a single writer per bridge. failed_blocks sums row widths directly, exact only because rows for a pair are disjoint and non-adjacent — an invariant maintained by merge-on-write within one writer. The single-writer assumption was already implicit in checkpointing (LEAST/GREATEST tolerate concurrency without making it correct); multi-writer would need an EXCLUDE USING gist non-overlap constraint before the cache could be trusted.

nodes.label: Gotcha: just test / just test-with-db Silently Target The Dev Database
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: just test / just test-with-db silently target the dev database
nodes.rationale: The justfile computes DATABASE_URL from DB_HOST/DB_PORT (defaulting to localhost:5432, the dev database) and exports it, overriding whatever the calling shell already set. just test-with-db manages a disposable Postgres on TEST_DB_PORT (9433) end to end and is the safe self-contained run; for a targeted run against a specific database, call cargo test directly with an explicit DATABASE_URL. test-with-db also runs one workspace-wide cargo test invocation, so an unrelated failing crate aborts the run — scope with cargo test -p <crate>.

nodes.label: Gotcha: One Scanner Per (bridge, chain), Never One Per Contract
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: one scanner per (bridge, chain), never one per contract
nodes.rationale: indexer_checkpoints, indexer_failures and the progress API are all keyed (bridge_id, chain_id), so two scanners on one chain share a scan frontier while each covers only part of the address set — and mark_catchup_complete lowers catchup_max_cursor with LEAST, so the first scanner to reach its floor publishes that floor for the whole pair. The invariant when adding a protocol is that the unit of scanning must match the key of the records that describe scanning. Scanning a wider address set or a lower floor than needed is free; splitting the scan under a shared key is not.

nodes.label: Gotcha: A Replay Can Only Recover What The Replay Can Still Find
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: a replay can only recover what the replay can still find
nodes.rationale: The ledger records block ranges and a replay re-fetches blocks, but anything the failed attempt consumed from memory — a correlation-queue entry, a lookup, a drained channel — is not restored, so the replay finds nothing, returns Ok, and resolve deletes the row. AMB's message-hash queue used to remove the pending entry before the fallible applies, losing the remainder on a mid-drain failure while the block was correctly recorded; both halves looked right in isolation. Consume in-memory state last: work on a clone and remove the original only after every fallible step succeeded, accepting at-least-once, which is already the regime for any replayed range.

nodes.label: Gotcha: Two Pre-Existing avalanche-e2e Failures Are Environmental, Not Regressions
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: two pre-existing avalanche-e2e failures are environmental, not regressions
nodes.rationale: Exactly two of nine avalanche-e2e tests fail reproducibly on any commit including main. test_home_chain_does_not_override_strict_unknown_filter polls for a chains/blockchain-ID mapping the resolver will never write for its scenario (it writes only when process_unknown_chains is set or the chain exists) — a test/contract mismatch, not a network problem. test_icm_and_ictt_are_indexed races the catch-up-exit checkpoint write in log_stream.rs: both chains are forked exactly at the event block so there is no catch-up range, the checkpoint reports done before the realtime fetch is handled, and the test's readiness check is checkpoint equality. Confirm they already fail on main rather than chasing them as regressions; fixing either is a separate pre-existing-bug task.
